title: 2008 AMC 10B Problem 20
statement: The faces of a cubical die are marked with the numbers \(1,\) \(2,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(3,\) and \(4.\) The faces of a second cubical die are marked with the numbers \(1,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) \(5,\) \(6,\) and \(8.\) Both dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum of the two top numbers will be \(5,\) \(7,\) or \(9?\)

solutions.text:
Of the \(36\) equally likely outcomes, the pairs giving sum \(5\) are \((1,4),(2,3),(2,3),(4,1),\) which is \(4\) outcomes.

Sum \(7\) comes from \((1,6),(2,5),(2,5),\) \((3,4),(3,4),(4,3),\) which is \(6,\) and sum \(9\) from \((1,8),(3,6),(3,6),(4,5),\) which is \(4.\)

The probability is \(\tfrac{4+6+4}{36}=\tfrac{14}{36}=\tfrac{7}{18}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: There are \(6\times 6=36\) equally likely outcomes; count those summing to \(5,7,\) or \(9\)
Remember each \(2\) and each \(3\) on the first die appears on two faces
